messages:
maria: Quick announcement: we're starting a small preview of ephemeral CI runners on AWS Fargate using OIDC-based tokenless auth. looking for 3-5 teams to opt in as canaries this week. details below.

jonathan: Sweet. Do we scope it to specific repos or teams?

maria: Repo-level canary. initial list: devex/ci-templates, infra/infra-templates, web-app/frontend, data/etl. we won't flip org-wide settings yet.

rahul: How are secrets accessed inside the runner? we still need encrypted parameters for deploy steps.

maria: Runners assume a short-lived role via OIDC; secrets fetched at runtime via ssm:GetParameter and decrypted with KMS. no PATs mounted. sample config: 
```
runners:
  executor: fargate
  auth: oidc
  role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-fargate-ephemeral
```

anna: Will tracing/log correlation work with our existing SRE dashboards? need to avoid blindspots.

jonathan: yes. they emit OTLP spans. i'll add the task-arn -> trace attribute mapper this afternoon.

sam: Cost concern: short jobs ok, but long parallel matrix builds may spike spend. is there a cap?

maria: preview autoscale: max 30 tasks per cluster. our current projection is ~+5% cost at peak. we'll review after a few days.

rahul: If Fargate runs out of capacity, what's the fallback?

maria: fallback route sends jobs to the legacy self-hosted runner pool (label: legacy). policy in devex/ci-routing repo. jobs won't be dropped.

anna: I'll update the CI runbook, include task drain, and mapping to instance logs.

jonathan: Can we gate per-repo with a feature flag or label? want to avoid accidental mass exposure.

maria: yes 00% gated by runner label `fargate-canary`. only repos with that label will pick ephemeral runners.

sam: i'll sign up web-app/frontend and run a full build tomorrow. ping me with the exact label to add.

ci-bot: build #4023 (web-app/frontend) succeeded on ephemeral-runner-7f3d :white_check_mark:

rahul: saw the logs. one noisy warning about file descriptors in the test container, but otherwise clean.

maria: logged a follow-up in devex/ci-ops with the excerpt and proposed fix.

jonathan: Note: keep infra/critical out until we validate cache warmups — they matter for infra tests.

maria: agreed, infra/critical excluded for now.

anna: What's the timeline for beta and broader rollout?

maria: Plan: preview this week, expand to beta in two weeks if no major issues, full rollout target in six weeks. we'll post a metrics summary after 72 hours of canary runs. :thumbsup:

sam: 44d

jonathan: i'll monitor perf metrics and report anomalies to #eng-sre.

maria: Thanks all. DM me if you want early access or help adding the repo label.
